 What we can offer you:

Sopho Pty Ltd as trustee for the Sopho Unit Trust trading as Kangaroo Valley Golf & Country Retreat, operates a distinctive accommodation and hospitality destination in the heart of Kangaroo Valley, NSW, within the Southern Highlands and South Coast region and an easy two-hour drive from both Sydney and Canberra. The Retreat is centred on a historic 1901 Woolshed — relocated from Uri Park in outback NSW and lovingly restored in 1983 — which today houses The Woolshed Restaurant and provides a characterful setting for guests and private functions alike. The property is complemented by an 18-hole championship golf course designed by Jack Newton, and by Osteria La Vallata, an Italian-inspired fine-dining restaurant led by Chef Marco Salvestrin.

Welcoming overnight guests, golf and leisure visitors, function and event parties, and regional tourists, Kangaroo Valley Golf & Country Retreat delivers a premium accommodation and hospitality experience across its accommodation, dining, and recreation offerings. As a destination property in a popular regional tourism location, the Retreat depends on attentive, individualised guest care and consistent day-to-day operational oversight to maintain its standing and the high standard of guest experience for which it is known.

As part of its continued growth, Sopho Pty Ltd is seeking to appoint a skilled and experienced Accommodation and Hospitality Manager in a permanent full-time position. The role is responsible for the overall administration and day-to-day operation of Kangaroo Valley Golf & Country Retreat, with a primary focus on accommodation services and the personalised guest experience across the property. The role offers a salary range of AUD $75,000 to AUD $85,000 per annum plus superannuation, commensurate with the successful candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience.

Job tasks and responsibilities
1.  Direct and oversee major accommodation - related operations such as reservations, reception, room service, and housekeeping activities across the property's 30 self-contained one-, two-, and three-bedroom cabins and villas, ensuring that turnaround, presentation, and guest check-in/check-out standards are consistently met.
2.  Plan and coordinate special functions, conferences and private events held in the Conference & Events Centre, liaising with clients on room setup, AV/presentation equipment and catering requirements.
3.  Coordinate closely with the Executive Chef to align front-of-house service delivery with kitchen output, executing and leading front-of-house service across Osteria La Vallata restaurant, in-room dining and event catering to deliver a seamless overall guest hospitality experience.
4.  Direct the Greenkeeper Superintendent and golf course maintenance team to ensure the 18-hole championship course and surrounding grounds are presented and maintained to the standard expected of guests and members.
5.  Supervise security arrangements and, through the Maintenance Manager, the upkeep of buildings, gardens, pools, tennis courts and other recreational facilities used by guests.
6.  Oversee the selection, training, rostering and supervision of accommodation, guest services, maintenance, golf course and other staff, and ensure compliance with occupational health and safety regulations across the site.
7.  Observe liquor licensing, food safety, health and other regulatory requirements relevant to the accommodation, restaurant, golf and function operations.
8.  Assess and review guest and customer satisfaction through feedback channels and online review platforms, and implement service improvements accordingly.
9.  Oversee purchasing and accounting activities related to accommodation, hospitality and course-maintenance operations, including supplier arrangements for housekeeping, maintenance, kitchen and guest amenities.
10.  Provide guests with local tourism information and coordinate golf, dining and activity bookings as part of the retreat experience, arranging tours or transport where required.
11.  Handle guest complaints and service escalations, negotiating with suppliers and other stakeholders to resolve issues, and conduct ongoing quality checks across accommodation, dining and event operations, initiating corrective action where standards are not met.
12.  Lead public relations and marketing initiatives to promote the Retreat and grow accommodation patronage
13.  Report on operational performance, staffing and guest service outcomes to the Operations Manager and General Manager, and contribute to forward operational planning, performance forecasting and risk management to support the retreat's ongoing service standards and growth.

How to join the team
To join our dedicated team for a rewarding career, please submit an online application. Only successful applicants will be contacted. Candidates must hold Australian or NZ Citizenship or have the capacity to permanently work in Australia. Employment of a temporary visa holder may only occur if no suitable permanent resident or citizen of Australia has been identified for this position following suitable labour market testing.

result.description:
Australian Fishing Enterprises (AFE) is the largest exporter of Southern Bluefin Tuna in Australia. Our tuna is exported around the world for sale in international marketplaces as a premium sushi/sashimi product. We specialise in the fishing, ranching and grow out of Southern Bluefin Tuna and control the entire process from catching to feeding, harvesting, processing and delivery. 
This position is available from November 2026 or sooner for suitable candidates with a valid AMSA Near Coastal Marine Engine Driver Grade 2/3 Certification, for a placement for up to 4 years.
Vessel Engineer Duties:
The Employee will be required to perform certain duties as listed below whilst at Sea (offshore) and on the Farm Site (inshore), although this list is not exhaustive it is a generalised overview of duties.
Engineer Duties:
•	Engine Room Watchkeeping 
•	Periodical Engine Servicing
•	Maintain machinery to an Operational capacity
•	Use of Pumping Systems
•	Vessel Slipping and Docking
•	Vessel Maintenance/Repairs 
•	Vessel Crane Operation
•	Refuelling & Bunkering
•	Loading and Unloading of vessel at Sea and On-shore
•	Reporting to Vessel Master
•	Maintenance and repairs coordinated with Fleet Manager
•	Forklift operation on-shore only (if Licensed)
•	Fish Feeding 
•	Repetitive Manual labour 
•	Vessel cleaning and house keeping 
•	Vessel Mooring/Berthing 
•	Net mending 
•	Rope work (Splicing, Knotting etc.)
•	Farm Pontoon Maintenance
Also including Deck Hand duties:
Deckhand Duties:
•	Ability to stand on unstable surfaces and undertake general duties on a day-to-day basis as advised by the Master 
•	Forklift operation (only if Licensed from previous deployment on SWP)  onshore only
•	Loading and Unloading of vessel at Sea and On-shore
•	Deck Machinery Operation
•	Fish Feeding 
•	Fish Processing and Packing
•	Maintenance as directed by Vessel Engineer
•	Repetitive Manual labour 
•	Vessel cleaning and house keeping 
•	Vessel Mooring/Berthing 
•	Net mending & Rope work (Splicing, Knotting etc.)
•	High Pressure Water Blasting
•	Painting by Hand and/or Spray
•	Farm Pontoon Maintenance
•	Portable hand tool use

The Employee will be required to perform the following additional duties whilst at Sea for Offshore Operations.
Navigation Watch:
• Keeping Lookout for other Vessels
• Maintaining Vessel Course as per Master’s instructions
• Vessel Log recording
• Watch Handover to next watch keeper
• Reporting to the Master
• Radio frequency monitoring
A Navigational watch can per performed at any time throughout the day or night, they are generally 1.5-2 hours in duration.

Additional Deck Duties:
• Tender vessel operation
• Launch and retrieval of tender
• Fish Sampling/Chumming
• Maintenance as directed by Vessel Engineer
• Repetitive Manual labour
• Vessel cleaning and house keeping
• Vessel Mooring/Berthing
*This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to the role.

Hours of operation are determined by the daily operational needs,.
January – July Operations are 7 days per week; you can work up to 6 days in a week. Up to 12 hours per day.
August to December Operations are 5 days per week Monday to Friday, you will work up to 5 days in a week, 8 hours per day.
Offshore Operations:
Tow & Support operations begin in December through to late March. If Quota is exhausted quickly the Offshore Operations will cease before late March.
Hours of operation whilst at Sea are from Sunrise to Sunset plus a navigational watch. 

Renumeration is paid as per the Award Rate, paid on a fortnightly basis. Farm work completed inshore and onshore will be calculated at the applicable hourly Farm rate. Aquaculture Award:(https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000114.html)(https://calculate.fairwork.gov.au/payguides/fairwork/ma000114/pdf)
OFFSHORE OPERATIONS
An additional contract is put in place alongside original Deckhand Contract to cover the periods Offshore for Tow & Support operations to classify Duties and Remuneration (there is no Award that covers the "At Sea" roles), contract renumeration is calculated from experience and seamanship knowledge.

This is not a FIFO position. Successful applicants will need to based in Port Lincoln for the duration of the contracted period.

result.description:
A busy, community-focused medical centre in tropical Far North Queensland is seeking a  General Practitioner  who is passionate about community medicine. Located in  Cairns , this  DPA-approved  practice has a high patient volume and has been providing medical care to the local community since 2011. 

 The predominately bulk-billing centre operates Monday to Friday with optional Sunday work. The facility is well-equipped with 11 consultation rooms, a four-bay treatment room, and a dedicated procedure room. Practitioners will join a collegial team of 11 doctors who have special interests in skin cancer medicine, family medicine, and Indigenous health, with a strong focus on providing medical care and advocacy for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients. An extensive administrative team and full-time nurses, who are trained in all treatment room and Chronic Disease Management (CDM) duties, provide support, allowing doctors to focus on practising medicine. 

 The practice provides clinical autonomy and flexible working arrangements. It is a registrar training facility with supervisor opportunities available. The practice's partnership with the RACGP simplifies the process of achieving and recording CPD requirements, with free in-house opportunities and discounted registration for industry events also provided. Practitioners with a special interest in skin, aesthetics, and occupational medicine are supported. The practice is backed by a major healthcare division, providing sophisticated IT, marketing, and finance services with 24-hour IT support, ensuring a smooth and efficient practice environment. Located in Cairns, the practice offers an excellent work-life balance in a region known for its extraordinary natural wonders, from the Great Barrier Reef to the Daintree Rainforest.   Apply Now
